lesson.title: Hannibal and the Second Punic War
lesson.goal: Follow Hannibal's march from Spain over the Alps into Italy, and see how Rome turned the war around by sailing to Africa.

say: In 218 BC, Carthage ruled from North Africa and held New Carthage in Spain. That year the Second Punic War with Rome began.
Hannibal marched from New Carthage, crossed the Pyrenees, and led his army and elephants over the Alps.
He swept down Italy, and in 216 BC he destroyed a Roman army at Cannae.
Rome did not give in. From 210 BC Scipio led its armies, carried the war to Africa, and in 202 BC beat Hannibal at Zama, near Carthage.
